name: Chai Stall
summary: A roadside tea stall: brew each order, lower the flame before it boils over, pour high and get paid
about: An evening tea stall under a striped awning and swinging string lights, with a keeper behind a painted counter, a chalk menu in PKR and a wall clock on real time. Orders arrive as paper tickets; you brew milk, cardamom or pink tea, catch the foam before it spills, then the keeper pours it high into the glass and a customer's hand takes it and leaves coins in the till. Good for a cafe or food page, a cosy loading scene or a playful order demo.
how: Read the ticket on the rail; the tea and rusk choices match it, or change them yourself.
Press Brew: leaves, milk and spice go in and it comes to the boil.
When the foam climbs to the rim, press Lower the flame (or tap the stove, or press F) twice; wait too long and it boils over.
Watch the high pour, the froth and the steam, then the customer pays and the till adds it up in PKR.
Ring the bell for a new customer, and move your pointer through the steam to swirl it.
